claims.claim_text: The indexed Romeo P Digiulian has a high-confidence match to an official Army record spelling the surname Di Giuliam.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The given name and initial agree; a nonshared protected identifier matches Army bulk record ordinal 4298009 despite the final-letter surname discrepancy.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from protected-identifier agreement; preserve the printed Digiulian and Army Di Giuliam spellings separately.
claims.temporal_assessment: Wartime Army identity only; neither a civilian employer nor OSS transfer date is supplied.
claims.match_notes: Do not silently correct the final letter or publish the protected identifier.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Konrad C Dillow has a high-confidence match to the University of Illinois graduate fellow and the World War II Army veteran described in a Washington Post obituary.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive full name appears in the official 1937 and 1938 university minutes; the obituary independently links the same full name to University of Illinois study and an Army parachute mission in France.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from distinctive full name, corroborating Illinois educational history, and wartime France service; Box 187 personnel file has not been examined.
claims.temporal_assessment: University fellowship is documented in 1937-38, before his wartime Army/OSS service; immediate predecessor remains unknown.
claims.match_notes: The obituary does not itself name OSS or a prewar employer; the fellowship is modeled separately as student status.

sources.locator_override: Konrad C. Dillow obituary, education and war-service paragraphs

claims.claim_text: Konrad C Dillow held a University of Illinois graduate fellowship in Education in 1937-38.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Official trustee minutes list Konrad C Dillow among graduate fellowship awardees in Education in April 1937 and record his resignation as a fellow effective February 1, 1938.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive full name and independent obituary linking the wartime veteran to University of Illinois graduate study.
claims.temporal_assessment: Clearly prewar, but a graduate fellowship is student status; it is not a verified university employer and is not shown to be immediately pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: Exclude this student affiliation from employer analytics. The 1939-42 WPA correspondence finding aid does not establish his job title or employer.
